work.sae_explanation: An SAÉ (Situation d'Apprentissage et d'Évaluation) is a project-based learning and assessment activity required to develop key professional competencies within the French higher education system.

pagil1.title: Creating a Game in the Terminal with Agile SCRUM Methodology
pagil1.text1: We had only a few days to create a game, following the agile Scrum methodology. Teams were formed randomly among all the members of the cohort. This allowed us to team up with people we didn’t know and to learn how to collaborate and communicate despite that.
pagil1.title2: Role of ScrumMaster, managing User Stories and tracking the project using the agile SCRUM methodology
pagil1.text2: During this project, each team member had a role, and I was assigned the role of Scrum Master. I was responsible for updating the progress board and creating burn-up and burn-down charts to show our project's progress.
pagil1.know_how3: communicate and collaborate in a team

pagil2.title: Creation of a BACK-END and a FRONT-END for a website
pagil2.presentationDescription: We only had a few days to create a website following the agile Scrum methodology. CodeSwipe is a parody application of Tinder where we replaced people with code snippets. Users swipe right if they think it's good code, or swipe left otherwise.
pagil2.role: Role of ScrumMaster, managing user stories and tracking the project using agile SCRUM methodology
pagil2.roleDescription: During this project, the role of ScrumMaster had to change every day. Therefore, I was responsible for updating the progress board and creating the burn-up chart. We paid more attention to managing tickets and Git branches during this project.
pagil2.know_how3: Communicate and collaborate in a team

sae103.title: Network Service Installation
sae103.presentationDescription: The primary goal of SAE 1.03 was to introduce us to network configuration, and SAE 2.03 aimed to teach us how to set up a network for a company and use Markdom or Ascii Doctor to write reports and documentation.
sae103.machine_install_text: We were instructed to install a virtual machine in two ways, one manually and one using a preconfigured file, to learn how to install operating systems on machines. This SAE required us to explore files and manuals to develop the skill of self-researching and finding the information we needed.
sae103.skill2: Configuring a workstation and collaborative network

sae105.title: Design and development of a website to present a company
sae105.presentation: Using HTML and CSS to create structure and design
sae105.presentationDescription: This project was about analyzing the needs of a company wanting to create an online platform for carpooling among their employees to address traffic and pollution issues. Based on this analysis, we had to design a mockup and then create a website that met these needs.
sae105.wordpress_text: We started by making a WordPress mockup to propose a beginning of design and solutions to the needs, and once it was validated, we moved on to the design directly in HTML and CSS. The main objective was to teach us how to code with these languages ​​in conditions similar to a real project as well as to make us respect a particular graphic charter, everything had to be coherent and enjoyable to look at.

sae202.title: Creating a School Exchange Application in Java and JavaFX
sae202.presentation: Development of an interactive application in Java
sae202.presentationDescription: The application was designed to allow student exchanges between countries. We needed to include a database of students based on countries and then calculate affinities based on specific parameters to match students with the most compatible partners, using graph algorithms like Dijkstra.
sae202.interface: Using JavaFX for the Human-Machine Interface
sae202.interface_description: This application was initially developed in a text format using the terminal. For the final version, we had to create a JavaFX application to give our program a graphical interface, making it more user-friendly and accessible.

sae207.title: Creating a Database - Data Breakdown
sae207.presentationDescription: We had to extract a large dataset from a file into a table and then process these data.
sae207.postgresql: Using PostgreSQL and Access to store and query data
sae207.postgresql_text: We used Postgresql and Access to create the tables and formulate the queries to be able to answer the 'client's' questions about the data.

sae213.title: Escape Game
sae213.presentationDescription: This SAE aimed to teach us teamwork and collaboration. Using Genially and Trello, which are collaborative tools, allowed us to better understand the importance of collaboration, even more so than in other group projects.
sae213.text1: We had to regularly organize meetings between all the team members. These meetings allowed us to take stock of the progress of the project, of the difficulties that a member might encounter, to provide help to those who needed it and to allow the emergence of new ideas through exchanges. We also had to document all the progress of the project and write the minutes of the meetings.
sae213.text2: We were asked to install and configure Gitea to set up a collaborative network and learn how to use it. Finally, we had to write a report to keep track of and explain everything we did. These reports had to be written in lightweight markup like Markdom or Ascii Doctor, which allowed us to gain the necessary skills to use lightweight markup languages.

sae302.title: Creating a Game with JavaFX
sae302.presentationDescription: We were given only gameplay instructions and some interface designs, and from that, we had to design the entire game. The game is played by two players: a monster and a hunter.
sae302.testingDescription: During this SAE, the professors particularly emphasized the relevance of the tests and documentation that we had to provide.

sae401.title: Developing a REST API
sae401.presentationDescription: This SAE focused on building a website for a pizzeria called 'Pizzeria Mazzorello' following the REST architecture.
sae401.security_description: Implementation of different authentication systems including API Token and JWT token.
sae401.skill1_text: We were not familiar with REST architectures, this project allowed us to understand them and learn how to create sites that respect them.
sae401.skill2_text: For this project, the use of a database was necessary.
sae401.know_how1_text: This project is the only one we had to do entirely alone, but being very independent, it didn't pose any problems for me.
sae401.know_how2_text: The deadlines for this project were quite short, it was a good exercise to be careful to deliver on time while respecting the specifications.

sae402.title: Development of a complex application
sae402.presentationDescription: We received a project brief with all the minimum features that the final application should include. Our first task was to come up with gameplay elements and a theme to match the given requirements.
sae402.multiplayer_description: This was the first time we had to develop a multiplayer game. It was a very interesting challenge and made us think and understand how multiplayer games work in general. Through this session, we learned how to use socket.iio to connect the server and clients, and to enable the creation of different independent games on the same server using rooms.
sae402.skill1_text: We had never coded in JavaScript before this project. It was an opportunity to learn and practice these new skills.
sae402.skill2_text: Using socket.io, we were able to create a multiplayer game where multiple games can take place at the same time.
sae402.skill3_text: Manage dependencies (package.json) in a js project.
sae402.skill4_text: Draw shapes, images on a canvas.
sae402.know_how1_text: We completed this project in pairs, which was originally planned to be done in threes, which put us to the test to finish on time with a third of our workforce.
sae402.know_how2_text: To complete the project on time, a good distribution of work was essential. We successfully met this challenge, meeting the specifications and even adding additional features.
sae402.know_how3_text: The professor had particularly insisted on the quality of our git repository and on task management, so we learned to better use GitLab's collaborative tools.

sae501.title: RiscV Emulator
sae501.presentationDescription: In this SAE, we faced the development of software that was beyond the usual scope we were accustomed to. We developed software that emulates a computer based on a RISC-V processor.
sae501.programmingDescription: Emulation is the process of simulating the operation of a hardware architecture using a computer program. The program is responsible for modeling and evolving the 'virtual' state of the hardware architecture. The emulation software must therefore provide a data structure that represents the hardware being simulated and evolve this data as the simulation progresses. Registers are the smallest storage units in the processor. They are integrated into the processor and have no address because they are not in memory. They can be used directly in machine instructions and serve as processing storage. The arithmetic and logic unit works exclusively with them on most architectures.
sae501.skill4: Writing a program that strictly follows specifications

sae509.title: WEB BACK
sae509.presentationDescription: The objective of this project was to create an appointment management website for multiple users.
sae509.spring_description: Spring is an open-source framework for building and defining the infrastructure of a Java application, facilitating its development and testing. Spring Boot is an open-source Java framework used to program standalone, production-quality Spring applications with a set of libraries that make it easier to start and manage projects. Through this project, we learned how to use the back-end Java framework Spring, as well as Spring Security. Spring Security is a Java/Java EE framework that provides authentication, authorization, and other security features for enterprise applications. Our project contains only two roles: User and Admin. An Admin can do everything a logged-in user can do, as well as access and modify other users' appointments.

first3dplatformer.title: Creating a game of my first 3D game: a platformer!
first3dplatformer.learn_godot_text: I started working on this game because I wanted to learn how to use Godot and create a 3D game. My first goal was to create a player with basic movement in a simple 3D environment. Then, step by step, I decided to continue with this simple gameplay mechanic and make a platformer game.
first3dplatformer.gameplay_elements_text: Continuing with this simple gameplay mechanic allowed me to focus on other aspects of the game, like creating menus with a pause and options menu. Also, I added new gameplay elements such as moving platforms, elevators, or collectibles in each level.

firstgamejam.title: My first game jam!
firstgamejam.title1: Post my first game on Itch.io
firstgamejam.text1: While browsing Itch.io, I saw the gamejam section and it made me want to participate. I chose the first gamejam that was about to start: 1-BIT JAM #4, and I started coding. I finished 114th out of 338 participants.
firstgamejam.text2: This game jam had one condition: the game could only contain two colors maximum, preferably black and white. I created TheLegendOfKnardWizight, a 2D shooter, following these constraints. The goal is to defend your tower from waves of monsters. If you get hit or if the tower is destroyed, you lose.

mazegenerator.title: Creating a maze generator.
mazegenerator.text1: I wanted to learn how to generate mazes. So I studied several algorithms that could do this, and then I tried to implement them.
mazegenerator.text2: At first, I displayed the mazes in the console in text form, then I decided to use JavaFX to represent my maze. It is from this personal project that I developed the display for the Saé 3.02 application development project.

minigames.title: Creation of a Pong and a brick breaker.
minigames.text1: I wanted to try creating a bunch of classic games, so after cloning Flappy Bird, I tried making a Pong and a Breakout clone. For each game I added a simple menu as well as a score and high score system.
minigames.text2: Creating these games allowed me to better understand game loops and JavaFX rendering.

miscellaneous.title: Other games in development.
miscellaneous.text: I enjoy trying to imagine how the user will react in order to create the best interface or a fun game. Sometimes I suddenly have an idea: a game concept, a solution to a problem in a project... and I can't stop thinking about it until I try to implement it.

matrices.text: I recently had fun making a page that does some matrix calculations, in order to practice using React.
